cards.b: A number with exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 1 is not prime; 2 is the only even prime.
Rational: can be written as a/b (integers, b ≠ 0), e.g. 0.125, √16. Irrational: decimal never ends or repeats, e.g. π, √2.

cards.f: How do you find the HCF from prime factors?
cards.b: Multiply the primes common to both numbers, using the lowest power of each.

cards.f: How do you find the LCM from prime factors?
cards.b: Multiply every prime that appears, using the highest power of each.

cards.f: What do you multiply by to rationalise 1/(a + √b)?
cards.b: The conjugate (a − √b). Then (a + √b)(a − √b) = a² − b, so the surd disappears.
